resolution: The comment in R/pillar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R no longer claims bit-for-bit agreement with the removed dense-inverse path; it says correctness rests on the covariance identity derived just above it and states what test-pillar7-bhs-fastpath.R actually checks (5-SD truth recovery, positive variance components, finite predictions). The neighbouring rcpp comment now states the measured draw-for-draw agreement instead of 'statistically equivalent'.

Measured first: under one seed the rcpp and gibbs backends agree draw for draw to ~1e-15 on beta, sigma2, tau2 and w_post_mean, with identical phi_hat, on three designs (slope, intercept only, three columns). test-pillar7-bhs-rcpp.R now asserts exactly that at tolerance 1e-8, replacing one posterior mean at tolerance 0.2 and the false comment that bit-equivalence could not be expected.

Measured with comments stripped from tests: 5 of 177 exports were never called. Each now has a test of what its help page promises: edaphos_example_profiles (synthetic flag, lattice, horizons belong to profiles, n cap, one-time notice), piml_profile_fit_mechanistic (layer mean checked against numerical quadrature on both branches, noise-free recovery, fixed surface, layer vs point mode, refusals), gnn_fit_ensemble (member k equals gnn_fit(seed = base + k), mean and sd of members, n = 1, NA mask), piml_neural_ode_predict and temporal_convlstm_predict (training-depth reproduction; return_sequence last step bit-identical). Each was checked to fail on a planted defect; one planted defect turned out to be equivalent code and is not counted.

Every entry point the action names now gives a message naming the function, the argument and the problem: quantum_krr_fit, piml_profile_fit, temporal_convlstm_fit and causal_estimate_effect replace raw stopifnot() text (and a mislabelled 'Covariates not found' for an unknown exposure; a character X used to pass with only a coercion warning). al_fit, al_loop and foundation_weights_load already did. test-error-messages.R gains a block per function, asserting the new messages.

One runtime guard, .require_torch() in R/core_utils.R, checks both the R package and a working libtorch (.torch_usable()); all nine sites that checked only requireNamespace('torch') call it. test-torch-guard.R simulates a machine with the package but no libtorch and asserts a clean refusal from five entry points; under the old guards those calls went ahead.

tests/testthat/test-print-snapshots.R snapshots 46 of the 48 print/summary methods (the other two are reached through them) with platform-volatile digits masked, recorded and checked stable across fresh processes. Reading the snapshots found seven print methods that misstated their object -- the DAG-test verdict without multiplicity correction, the GAT loss from an epoch whose weights were not returned, the Bayesian profile sigma labelled as a natural-scale posterior summary, an unconditional 'likely confounded', and three count or format errors -- all fixed in b939995 with unit tests that fail on the old output.

Duplicate ^\.claude$ removed; dead ^README\.Rmd$ removed; ^RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3\.10\.0\.md$ and ^RELEASE\.md$ replaced by ^RELEASE.*\.md$; the redundant ^paper/S2_File_pipeline\.zip$ (covered by ^paper$) removed. codecov.yml was already excluded. R CMD check --as-cran on bce5dab: 2 NOTEs, both environmental (new submission; local HTML Tidy too old).

Both third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs with the version beside them: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action (the job with contents: write) and codecov/codecov-action. .github/dependabot.yml (github-actions, monthly) keeps the pins current. R package versions are not pinned beyond DESCRIPTION's floors, which is the norm for a package as opposed to an application; the Dockerfile keeps its CRAN snapshot.
cd /path/to/GeoVersa is now cd /path/to/edaphos. The hand-off file, named after a phantom version, was renamed V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md -> tools/pretrain/ENCODER_V2_HANDOFF.md in 5141f9d.

The pkgdown navbar gains a Cheatsheets entry linking to cheatsheets/ on GitHub, and cheatsheets/README.md now says exactly that (linked from the site, not rendered by it). INTRO.md no longer says P9 has a task-appropriate benchmark: it says P2, P3 and P8 are compared against baselines in their vignettes and that P9's checks only the trivial-null loss.

The EDAPHOS_USE_MOCO_V2 branch, which only raised 'not yet implemented' inside a tryCatch and fell back to proxies, is removed. The script's header now says it is step 1 of 2: it writes the synthetic-DGP slots that data-raw/causal_iv_cerrado_rebuild.R keeps, and running it alone reverts causal_iv_cerrado.rds to the proxy analysis.

The four 'not written yet' markers point at the torch files that fulfilled them; the pillar 7 stop() message no longer names a version (and in 5141f9d the spBayes branch it guarded predicts, from PR #9); the dead pred_fn assignment in R/piml_quantum_bridge.R is deleted; the unreachable HTTP-status check in foundation_weights_download() is made live with req_error(is_error = FALSE) and deletes the partial file, tested with a mocked 404. Phantom vN.N.N labels are gone from R/, src/, tests, docs and data-raw except sentences that explain them.

package_v2_for_zenodo.R checks the checkpoint first, with a message carrying the resume command for a missing state.rds and for an undertrained encoder; the sprintf now has one format per argument; the artefact checks follow and say what to re-run; it stops instead of calling install.packages(). wire_up_v2_doi.R refuses to run before 200 000 steps.
The README carries no phantom version labels: release headings, the version column and the status cells are gone, so the two schemes no longer meet. Only real tags (v0.1.0-v1.6.0) and 2.0.0 remain.
DESCRIPTION is 2.0.0 and NEWS.md is one development entry; the README roadmap is the 'Releases and roadmap' section, without version-numbered rows (bce5dab removed the rest).
_pkgdown.yml has no hand-maintained release list (the site renders NEWS.md, and real releases are on GitHub) and its description says ten pillars.
.zenodo.json carries version 2.0.0 and a description rewritten for what ships, negative results included.

The badge and citation use the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19683708, which resolves to the latest version (v1.6.0 until 2.0.0 is deposited); the README no longer says it resolves to v0.2.0, and the 'Releases and roadmap' section lists what was deposited.

The weights registry has a status column; the v2 row is 'planned', and foundation_weights_list() hides it unless include_planned = TRUE, so the default list offers only an encoder with a URL, DOI and checksum. The hand-off placeholders are XXXXXXXX and wire_up_v2_doi.R requires a numeric Zenodo DOI.
As F0F5D47: the all-NA v2 row is marked planned and not offered by default; test-foundation-weights.R asserts the default list has no NA url, doi or sha256.

PR #9: bhs_fit(backend = 'spBayes') carries the same fields as the other backends, predict() delegates to spBayes::spPredict(), as_edaphos_posterior() and al_query_bhs() accept it; phi_method records profile-MLE vs posterior median. Tested in test-pillar7-bhs-spbayes.R.
bhs_fit's @param backend documents all three backends and what each does with phi; al_query_bhs() gates on the fields it reads, so rcpp fits are served (PR #9).
PR #9: a failed raster read or a patch over NoData gives an NA row with a warning, not an embedding of channel means; max_na_share (default 0.5) and attribute na_share make the tolerance explicit.
PR #9: quantum_kernel() refuses reps that is not a whole number >= 1 (reps = 0 returned an all-ones kernel) in R and in C++, and both backends stop before allocating more than 8 GB of state vectors.

No text claims a run larger than the ~100-abstract corpus of data-raw/run_large_corpus.R: the README heading and the llm_kg_pipeline_run() roxygen now say what has been run. The pkgdown group for the three benchmark_fit_* wrappers no longer calls them the 6-pillar set. The underlying work -- a 10k-abstract run -- is not done and is not claimed.
